item.name: 00 Measurement Contract
item.description:
# AIEI Measurement Contract

## The Story

This collection is the integrity layer of the AIEI framework. Before any scoring collection computes a number, the Measurement Contract validates six non-negotiable prerequisites that ensure your scores will be meaningful, comparable, and defensible.

Why does this matter? Because a score without context is just a number. If you compute an R-Score without confirming that a baseline cohort exists, you have no reference point. If you calculate a C-Score without verifying criticality weightings, you're treating all services as equally important — which they're not. The Measurement Contract prevents these silent errors by failing loudly before bad data enters the pipeline.

Think of it as a contract between the data and the scoring engine: "I promise these conditions are true before I ask you to calculate anything."

## The Seven Requests

### 1. Attribution Check
Verifies that every data source feeding into AIEI scores has a clear owner and origin. Unattributed data is untraceable data, and untraceable data has no place in an engineering effectiveness measurement.

### 2. Baseline Cohort Validation
Confirms that a baseline cohort (the reference group against which all scores are compared) is defined and populated. Without a baseline, scores have no relative meaning.

### 3. Criticality Weighting Check
Validates that services have been assigned criticality weights. These weights determine how much each service contributes to composite scores — missing weights mean silent miscalculations.

### 4. Join Completeness
Ensures that data from different sources (CI/CD, incident management, deployment logs) can be joined correctly. Incomplete joins produce partial scores that look valid but aren't.

### 5. Guardrail Coverage
Checks that guardrails (thresholds and boundaries) are defined for each metric. Guardrails prevent impossible or nonsensical scores from propagating through the system.

### 6. Anti-Vanity Compliance
Validates that the metrics being measured are actionable, not vanity metrics. This check enforces the AIEI principle that every metric must drive a decision or it doesn't belong in the framework.

### 7. Contract Verdict
Aggregates the results of checks 1–6 into a single pass/fail verdict. If any check fails, the verdict is FAIL and downstream scoring collections should not be run until the issue is resolved.

## What Comes Next
→ [04 AIEI R-Score: Reliability](collection/20784047-92a6734d-2913-4884-914f-8f608b94a209) to compute reliability scores
→ [05 AIEI Q-Score: Quality](collection/20784047-f54b97e6-2d8a-4c39-b4fe-3fd00fcc76f5) to compute quality scores
→ [08 AIEI Composite Score](collection/20784047-eee9821c-0e35-482d-98f0-b8971125960d) to combine all individual scores

item.name: 01 R-Score: Reliability
item.description:
# AIEI R-Score: Reliability

## The Story

Reliability is the first question any engineering leader should ask about AI-generated code: **"Does it break things?"**

The R-Score measures whether AI-assisted code is production-safe. It doesn't care how fast the code was written or how clever it is — only whether it survives contact with real users. The formula is deliberately multiplicative: `R = (1 − CFR) × SLO × Contract × Uptime × Adaptability`. Every factor must be strong for the score to hold. A team with perfect uptime but zero contract test coverage will still score poorly, because untested reliability is just luck.

This is the gateway score for most organizations because it uses Postman-native signals — collection failure rates, SLO compliance, contract test results — so you can compute it without any external integrations. If you can only measure one thing, measure this.

## The Pipeline

### 1. Fetch CFR & Reliability Metrics
Pulls the Critical Failure Rate and supporting reliability signals from the mock server (or real monitoring endpoints if configured). CFR is the percentage of deployments that cause a production incident within 24 hours.

### 2. Compute R Score
Applies the multiplicative formula and classifies the result: Strong (≥ 0.85), Moderate (0.60–0.84), Weak (0.40–0.59), or Critical (< 0.40). Stores the score and classification in the environment for use by the Composite Score and Executive Report collections.

## Key Signals
- **CFR** — Critical Failure Rate (lower is better)
- **SLO Compliance** — percentage of SLO targets met
- **Contract Coverage** — percentage of APIs with contract tests
- **Uptime** — service availability
- **Adaptability** — how quickly reliability recovers after AI-related incidents

## What Comes Next
→ [05 AIEI Q-Score](collection/20784047-f54b97e6-2d8a-4c39-b4fe-3fd00fcc76f5) to measure code quality
→ [08 AIEI Composite Score](collection/20784047-eee9821c-0e35-482d-98f0-b8971125960d) to combine all scores

item.name: 02 Q-Score: Quality
item.description:
# AIEI Q-Score: Quality

## The Story

Speed without quality is just faster failure. The Q-Score asks: **"Is AI-generated code actually good?"**

It measures three things that matter after code ships: how many defects it introduces, whether tests still pass, and how often it needs to be rewritten. These aren't proxy metrics — they're the outcomes that determine whether AI is helping your team or creating a cleanup backlog.

The formula `Q = (1 − DefectDelta) × TestPassDelta × (1 − ReworkDelta)` is designed to detect a common anti-pattern: AI that generates code quickly but creates a "trust-but-verify tax" where engineers spend more time reviewing and fixing AI output than they would have spent writing it themselves.

## The Pipeline

### 1. Fetch Defect Rates
Compares defect rates in AI-assisted code vs. human-written code. The delta tells you whether AI is introducing more bugs.

### 2. Fetch Test Pass Rate Delta
Measures whether test pass rates change when AI-generated code enters the codebase. A negative delta means AI code is harder to test or breaks existing tests.

### 3. Fetch Rework Rate
Tracks how often AI-generated code is modified within 14 days of merging. High rework suggests the code was accepted prematurely.

### 4. Compute Q Score
Combines all three signals into a single quality score. Classifications: Strong (≥ 0.85), Moderate (0.60–0.84), Weak (0.40–0.59), Critical (< 0.40).

## What Comes Next
→ [06 AIEI L-Score](collection/20784047-e99590a7-3b6a-4f87-876c-b311fd9c5ae7) to measure delivery speed
→ [08 AIEI Composite Score](collection/20784047-eee9821c-0e35-482d-98f0-b8971125960d) to combine all scores

item.description:
# AIEI L-Score: Lead Time

## The Story

This is the metric everyone *thinks* they're already measuring — but almost nobody measures correctly. The L-Score doesn't ask "Is AI making us faster?" It asks: **"Is AI making us faster without creating systemic bottlenecks?"**

The distinction matters. A team that ships PRs 40% faster but creates a review bottleneck (because every AI PR needs extra scrutiny) hasn't actually improved. The L-Score captures this by comparing AI-assisted vs. non-AI PR cycle times, factoring in agent mode efficiency, and using DORA deployment throughput as a regression check. If individual PRs are faster but overall throughput drops, the score reflects that.

## The Pipeline

### 1. Fetch PR Cycle Times
Compares median PR cycle time for AI-assisted PRs vs. human-only PRs. The ratio reveals whether AI is genuinely accelerating delivery or just shifting work between stages.

### 2. Fetch Agent Mode & DX Times
Measures developer experience metrics specific to AI tooling: time-in-agent-mode, context-switch frequency, and developer satisfaction signals.

### 3. Fetch DORA Throughput
Pulls deployment frequency as a system-level regression check. This is the guardrail that catches "fast PRs, slow deployments" — a pattern where individual velocity improves but system throughput doesn't.

### 4. Compute L Score
Combines PR speed, DX efficiency, and DORA throughput into a single lead time score. The DORA factor acts as a ceiling — you can't score higher than your deployment throughput supports.

## What Comes Next
→ [07 AIEI C-Score](collection/20784047-ced6cae3-a778-41c6-b582-cbdeacabf87f) to measure cost efficiency
→ [08 AIEI Composite Score](collection/20784047-eee9821c-0e35-482d-98f0-b8971125960d) to combine all scores

item.name: 04 C-Score: Cost Efficiency
item.description:
# AIEI C-Score: Cost Efficiency

## The Story

The C-Score answers the question that keeps CFOs up at night: **"Are we getting our money's worth from AI?"**

It computes raw ROI — labor value saved minus total AI costs (licenses, compute, training, integration) — and normalizes it against a configurable target. A score of 1.0 means you're hitting your ROI target exactly. Above 1.0 means AI is delivering more value than expected. Below 1.0 means you're paying more than you're getting.

The formula is deliberately transparent: `ROI = (labor_value_saved − total_ai_cost) / total_ai_cost`, then `C = min(ROI / target_roi, 1.0)`. There's no hidden weighting or subjective adjustment. If the math says you're losing money, the score says you're losing money.

## The Pipeline

### 1. Fetch Labor & Cost Data
Pulls labor value saved (hours × rate for AI-assisted work), AI licensing costs, compute costs, training costs, and integration overhead. In mock mode, uses representative values. In real mode, connects to your cost tracking systems.

### 2. Compute C Score
Calculates ROI, normalizes against target, and classifies: Strong (≥ 0.85), Moderate (0.60–0.84), Weak (0.40–0.59), Critical (< 0.40). A Critical C-Score is a red flag that AI investment isn't paying off — yet.

## What Comes Next
→ [08 AIEI Composite Score](collection/20784047-eee9821c-0e35-482d-98f0-b8971125960d) to combine all four scores
→ [09 AIEI Executive Report](collection/20784047-f3dae730-c7fc-4796-a387-a95361326551) to generate the CIO briefing

item.name: 05 Composite Score
item.description:
# AIEI Composite Score

## The Story

Four scores become one. The Composite Score is the single number that represents your organization's AI effectiveness — the figure that goes on the executive slide, the one that gets tracked quarter over quarter, the one that answers **"How are we doing?"** in a single breath.

The formula is a weighted average: `AIEI = wQ×Q + wL×L + wR×R + wC×C`, where the weights are configurable via the Setup Wizard. The default profile weights all four dimensions equally (25% each), but the framework supports custom profiles: reliability-heavy for platform teams, speed-heavy for product teams, cost-heavy for budget-constrained organizations.

The composite also carries a classification (Strong / Moderate / Weak / Critical) and a data confidence indicator that reflects how much of the score is based on real data vs. mock data. A high composite with low confidence is a warning, not a celebration.

## The Pipeline

### Compute AIEI Composite
Reads the four sub-scores (R, Q, L, C) from the environment, applies the configured weight profile, computes the weighted average, classifies the result, and stores everything back in the environment. This is the request that the Executive Report, Trend Analysis, and Team Comparison collections all depend on.

## What Comes Next
→ [09 AIEI Executive Report](collection/20784047-f3dae730-c7fc-4796-a387-a95361326551) to generate the CIO-ready briefing
→ [10 AIEI Trend Analysis](collection/20784047-e05d5ba1-0b40-4516-b49c-847014774d3f) to track changes over time

item.description:
# AIEI Falsifiability Watchdog

Detects situations where AI activity metrics can look positive while system outcomes degrade.

## Why this collection exists
AIEI is only defensible if it can fail. If we cannot detect contradictory signals, we do not have a measurement system - we have a narrative.

## Detectors
1. **Velocity-Quality Divergence** - faster delivery while quality drops
2. **Trust-But-Verify Tax** - review overhead cancels AI speed gains
3. **Cost Inflation** - AI costs rising while ROI stalls
4. **Interface Drift** - API contract drift despite passing local workflows
5. **Guardrail Erosion** - governance controls weakening over time
6. **Watchdog Summary Dashboard** - consolidated executive falsifiability view

exec: ? 'Velocity improvements are not translating to system quality outcomes.'
: 'No divergence pattern detected at current thresholds.';
// Proxy estimate: if lead-time gain is low and ROI is weak, review overhead is likely eating gains.

: 'No interface drift warning at current coverage and score thresholds.';
